name: Winona LaDuke
shortBio: Anishinaabe (Ojibwe) environmental philosopher, economist, and land sovereignty activist whose work articulates Indigenous ecological governance, the Eighth Fire prophecy, and legal defense of ancestral seed and water commons.
centralQuestion: How can Indigenous relational sovereignty and Seventh-Generation ethics dismantle extractive fossil capitalism ("Waniikwe" / ecological amnesia)?

keyWorks.title: All Our Relations: Native Struggles for Land and Life
keyWorks.description: Examines environmental racism across Indigenous nations, grounding restorative ecology in reciprocal kinship with the living world.

keyWorks.title: Recovering the Sacred: The Power of Naming and Claiming
keyWorks.description: Articulates Anishinaabe land ethics, manoomin (wild rice) seed sovereignty, and resistance to biopiracy and extractivism.
